correctness.rationale: Ronda's sharp theorem supplies the common premise that every maximizer on the stated nondegenerate sphere has constant modulus. Equality in the convolution Cauchy–Schwarz step then requires phase alignment within every fiber of the pair-sum map. For \(q=3\), the sphere consists of the six signed coordinate vectors and the pair-sum relations have rank two, leaving four phase parameters up to no further constraint, equivalently equality of the three antipodal products. For \(q=5\), the radius-two sphere has twenty points. A fresh construction of all pair-sum phase relations produced a 109 by 20 integer relation matrix of rank 19 whose Smith invariants are sixteen ones followed by three fives, hence index \(125=5^3\) in the sum-zero lattice. The additive-character moment map has the same index and lies in the relation kernel, forcing equality. This independently reproduces the phase classification rather than relying on a finite numerical fit.
risks: The classification is only for the two stated small fields/radii; it does not claim the same phase law for all admissible finite fields.

final_claim: For the anisotropic three-dimensional sphere extension problem in the first two admissible small fields, the equality phases bifurcate: on \(\mathbb F_3^3\) with radius one, maximizers are exactly constant-modulus functions whose products agree on each antipodal pair, whereas on \(\mathbb F_5^3\) with radius two, every maximizer is a scalar multiple of an additive character.
limitations: Only the stated anisotropic three-dimensional spheres over \(\mathbb F_3\) and \(\mathbb F_5\).
